newsitem.title: THAILAND: GOLF-ELS LIFTS SUPER TOUR TITLE IN PLAY-OFF WITH WOOSNAM.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS LIFTS SUPER TOUR TITLE IN PLAY-OFF WITH WOOSNAM.

text.p: World number three Ernie Els of South Africa won the Johnnie Walker Super Tour title on Sunday after Welshman Ian Woosnam missed a seven-foot putt at the first play-off hole.
Els and Woosnam fought a low-scoring duel but both came unstuck in the closing stretch at the Thana City course to take the country-hopping tournament into an extra hole.

Former U.S. Masters champion Woosnam bogeyed the final hole yet still set a course record of 63 for a four-round total of 14-under-par 274. Els had a double bogey seven at the par-five 16th with the title seemingly in his grasp.

With his girlfriend Liezl Wehmeyer acting as caddy after his local bag carrier went sick, Els drove into a bunker and then found the water's edge with his second shot to lose two strokes and stand equal with Woosnam.
He parred the final two holes for a 65 and two-putted for victory at the first play-off hole.

"It is a really brilliant feeling to have won," said the 27-year-old Els. "It has been a long week flying about Asia but also a fun week. The scores today were just great -- it is tough to get to a golf course and play it blind but everybody did well.
"I thought I played really well today -- normally a 65 in the final round when you are holding a two-shot lead would be enough but Woosie is a class player and it went to a play-off."
Woosnam, second on the European circuit, said hot weather finally took its toll at the play-off hole.
"It has been hard work this week and I was really tired after nine holes today but playing well kept me going. Being competitive and trying to catch up with Ernie spurred me on," he said.
Els started the final round on seven-under-par 209, two ahead of Woosnam and Colin Montgomerie of Scotland.
After beginning with a five-under-par 67 at the Ta Shee Golf and Country Club in Taiwan, he recorded back-to-back 71s at Seoul Country Club and the Orchard Golf and Country Club in Manila.
Woosnam beat the old course record of 64 jointly held by Brandt Jobe of the United States and Mexico's Carlos Espinosa.
Montgomerie shot a last-round 69 to finish six off the pace in the eight-player field.
